notes: 2026-02-24 — Onsite session with product + infra (CTO present). Focus: Dedicated for predictable latency and cost control. Quote from CTO: "we need predictable tail latency during launch windows".
Product use-case: in-app assistant for pro users (support + in-product guidance) + embeddings for search relevance across 200M docs. Need reranking for top-N precision in search results.

Latency targets: p95 < 300ms for single-turn chat at 512 tokens, burst spikes ok for 10 minutes but mustn't exceed 20% error rate. Throughput target: sustained 120 qps across primary region, spikes to 400 qps during launches.
POC scope: validate Dedicated pool with 2 reserved GPU nodes (A100 equivalent), test autoscaling to burst capacity and KV cache warmup. Measure cost/tok and quality drift vs open models.

Pricing convo summary: customer prefers Dedicated commit + burst credits model. Asking for three-tier commit examples: 250k tokens/day, 1M tokens/day, 5M tokens/day. Wants clear overage pricing and predictable monthly invoice.

Redwood proposal items discussed: committed vCPU/GPU hours, baseline throughput, burst buckets (minute-level tokens), overage rate (proposed 1.5x on-commit unit price), ramp schedule (3-month ramp to full commit), canary rollback SLA.

Negotiation notes: customer pushing for lower overage multiplier (1.2x) and larger initial burst quota. Legal flagged MSA indemnity clause and data residency addendum. Procurement asked for 12-month commit with quarterly ramp credits.
Security: must support SSO/SAML, KMS integration for model keys, audit logs retention 1 year. They will require a short security review board session next week (linked SEC-2104).
Engineering question: how does Redwood route between hosted fallback and Dedicated during maintenance? Customer wants automatic routing to regional hosted API with model pinning preserved.

Action items from 2026-03-01 call: SE to produce cost model spreadsheet showing commit vs burst vs pay-as-you-go; AE/Jordan to get legal template for MSA; propose two committed tiers with ramp schedule and demonstrable cost savings vs hosted.
Quote from Product Lead: "If we can lock a predictable unit cost and keep p95 below 300ms, we can roll to 20k users in Q3."
Customer timeline: target sign in 2026-04, POC end 2026-03-15, pilot rollout in Q2. Forecasted ARR contingent on Dedicated pricing acceptance and security signoff.
